top_findings.title: POST /books does not create or persist a book
top_findings.evidence: app.py:11-12 create_book returns jsonify({'message':'Book created successfully'},201); request body is never read (no request.get_json()) and nothing is stored.
top_findings.suggestion: Read the JSON body, validate it, and INSERT into the SQLite books table; return the created book with 201.

top_findings.title: GET /books has no ?author= filter
top_findings.evidence: app.py:14-22 list_books returns a hard-coded single-book list; request.args is never consulted, so ?author= is ignored.
top_findings.suggestion: Read request.args.get('author') and filter the query/collection by it.

top_findings.title: No SQLite/embedded persistence
top_findings.evidence: app.py:1 imports sqlite3 but it is the only reference — grep finds no connect/cursor/execute/CREATE TABLE/INSERT/SELECT anywhere; all handlers return hard-coded literals.
top_findings.suggestion: Add a real SQLite layer: create the books table, and back every CRUD route with it.

top_findings.title: No input validation for required title/author
top_findings.evidence: app.py:11-12 create_book never inspects the body; a POST missing title/author is not rejected with 400.
top_findings.suggestion: Validate that title and author are present in the JSON body; return 400 otherwise.

top_findings.title: Only 2 tests present (requirement is >= 3)
top_findings.evidence: test_app.py defines 2 test methods (test_health_check, test_create_book); grep -c 'def test_' == 2, below the required 3.
top_findings.suggestion: Add at least one more test to meet the >=3 threshold.
